# MCP tool reference

The exact signature of every tool an agent sees: **14 tools**, generated from the MCP server's own `list_tools()` response, so it cannot drift from the code. Each tool's text is reproduced verbatim — it is what the agent reads when deciding which tool to call.

See [MCP server](/mcp) for connecting a client, the response envelope, the token budget and the server instructions.

::: info Where the bounds come from
The schema an agent receives is derived from the handler signature, so it carries types and defaults but **no** bounds. The bounds column comes from the argument model the server validates against: exceeding one is a validation error, not a silent truncation — with the single exception noted on `cograph_retrieve`.

Rules that span two parameters cannot live in a per-parameter table, so they appear as bullets under it. Read those before calling a tool whose arguments are all optional: `cograph_outline` has two, and requires exactly one.
:::

## Orientation

Called first, to find out what exists and where to look. Cheap — these return names, structure and scores rather than ranked search results. `cograph_repository_readme` is the one that returns a document body, because knowing what a repository is for is the point of orienting.

### `cograph_repositories`

List repositories readable by the authenticated MCP user. Returns compound slugs (host/owner/name) and the wiki resource URI. There is no graph resource URI — use cograph_search_code / cograph_read_node / cograph_related for the graph.

Use when: you know a repository only by name (pass search=name) or need the list; feed the host/owner/name slug into the other tools.

Do NOT use to read a repo's docs (use cograph_repository_readme) or to search inside a repo (use cograph_retrieve / cograph_search_code).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | string | no | — | — |
| `status` | `pending` \| `cloning` \| `indexing` \| `embedding` \| `generating` \| `ready` \| `error` \| `deleting` | no | — | — |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` | ≥ 1 |

### `cograph_collections`

List markdown collections readable by the authenticated MCP user.

Use when: target collection_id is unknown — start here to enumerate.

Do NOT use to read a collection's documents (use cograph_collection_document) or to search inside a collection (use cograph_collection_search).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | string | no | — | — |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` | 1–100 |

### `cograph_route`

Rank the repositories and markdown collections most likely to hold the answer to a natural-language query. Returns up to `top_k` candidates per kind with a rough `score` in [0, 1] and a one-line `why`.

Use when: the question does not name a repository and you do not know which one holds the answer. Optional: skip it when you know the repository. Use the top 1-2 candidates; scores are rough.

Do NOT use when the repository is known (go straight to cograph_search_code or cograph_retrieve), and do NOT use instead of cograph_retrieve: route returns pointers to sources, not code.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | yes | — | non-empty, ≤ 512 chars |
| `top_k` | integer | no | `3` | 1–10 |

### `cograph_outline`

Token-cheap structural overview: top-level dirs + wiki page titles for a repo, OR document titles + heading sketches for an md collection. ≤ 30 items per section.

Use when: you need to see what a repository or collection holds, or a wiki page slug for cograph_wiki_page (`wiki_pages`). Optional; skip it when you can search directly.

Do NOT use to read content (use cograph_repository_readme / cograph_collection_document) or to search (use cograph_retrieve).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | string | no | — | — |
| `collection_id` | uuid | no | — | — |

- Pass **exactly one** of `repository` or `collection_id`. Both optional in the schema, but omitting both — or supplying both — is an `INVALID_REQUEST` error.

### `cograph_repository_readme`

Fetch the canonical README/Overview document for a repository in one call.

Use when: the agent has a repo slug and wants to know what the project does, its scope, or how to use it. Only the README at the repository's tree root counts; a nested one describes something narrower. Falls back to the compacted wiki Overview (lead + section headings) when there is none.

Do NOT use to search inside the readme (use cograph_retrieve mode='wiki') or to read other docs (use cograph_collection_search / cograph_read_chunk).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | — |

## Search

Ranked candidates within one source. Returns snippets, not whole files.

### `cograph_retrieve`

Hybrid search across the code and checked-in docs of one repository. Returns one record per place: a code hit as {node_id, name, at: path:start-end, called_by, code}, a doc as {heading_path, at, text}.

`code` is a query-anchored excerpt, not the whole body: up to ~600 chars for the first 3 hits, ~160 for the rest. Read the best one or two hits with cograph_read_node(node_id) or their `at` with cograph_read_file_range.

`called_by` lists up to 3 callers {name, at}; called_by_more counts the rest; [] means no callers. When a hit is only a helper, follow called_by to the code that uses it.

`repository` is required, as host/owner/name. Unknown repository: pick one with cograph_repositories or cograph_route. `top_k` bounds the results (clamped to 25); the default 10 is usually enough.

No hits and a code name in the query: `next` is the cograph_search_code call to run.

`wiki` (only when a generated-wiki page covers the hits) lists up to 2 pages {page, title, lead}; read one with cograph_wiki_page(page).

Use when: a question in words, one topic per call. mode='code' for 'where is X implemented'. mode='wiki' searches the repository's checked-in docs (README, docs/), not the generated wiki. mode='mixed' when unsure.

Do NOT use for a name from the code (use cograph_search_code) or to read a known node fully (use cograph_read_node).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | yes | — | non-empty |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | non-empty |
| `mode` | `code` \| `wiki` \| `mixed` | no | `mixed` | — |
| `stores` | (`ast` \| `code` \| `ast_summary` \| `repo_doc`)[] | no | — | — |
| `top_k` | integer | no | `10` | ≥ 1, silently clamped to 25 |
| `snippet_chars` | integer | no | `600` | 80–4000 |
| `as_of` | date-time | no | — | — |
| `since` | date-time | no | — | — |
| `until` | date-time | no | — | — |
| `include_chunks` | boolean | no | `true` | — |
| `include_graph` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `include_scores` | boolean | no | `false` | — |

- `since` must be earlier than or equal to **both** `until` and `as_of`.
- A non-empty `stores` replaces the layer set `mode` would have selected. An empty list is accepted and ignored — `mode` still decides — so omit `stores` rather than passing `[]` to mean “nothing”.

### `cograph_search_code`

Lexical + fuzzy symbol search over a repository's code nodes. Returns at most 25 records {node_id, name, at: path:start-end, called_by, code}, where `code` is the signature, not the body. Pick the right node, then read it with cograph_read_node(node_id).

`called_by` lists up to 3 callers {name, at}; called_by_more counts the rest; [] means no callers.

No hits: `reason` names the words searched for.

`wiki` (only when a generated-wiki page covers the hits) lists up to 2 pages {page, title, lead}; read one with cograph_wiki_page(page).

path_prefix (a folder from the repository root, e.g. internal/shipping/) keeps only hits under it.

Use when: you have a word from the code: a name (class, function, qualified path) or a word that appears in the code. `repository` is host/owner/name.

Do NOT use for natural-language questions (use cograph_retrieve with mode=code) or to read a node fully (use cograph_read_node).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | — |
| `query` | string | yes | — | non-empty |
| `top_k` | integer | no | `10` | ≥ 1 |
| `path_prefix` | string | no | — | — |

### `cograph_collection_search`

Hybrid search inside one readable markdown collection. Returns query-anchored excerpts (snippet + content_truncated) per chunk with a top-level total_tokens_estimate.

Use when: you have a collection_id and a question for team docs: what a term means, a product rule, why something was decided.

Do NOT use to search code/wiki across repositories (use cograph_retrieve) or to read a chunk fully (use cograph_read_chunk).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collection_id` | uuid | yes | — | — |
| `query` | string | yes | — | non-empty |
| `top_k` | integer | no | `10` | 1–100 |
| `snippet_chars` | integer | no | `600` | 80–4000 |

## Read

Exact content for something already identified by a search or an outline.

### `cograph_read_node`

Read one code node's exact source (a function, method or type) with its AST citation. The body keeps its real lines from provenance.start_line, at most snippet_chars (default 6000, max 16000) cut on a line boundary; if `content_truncated`, continue with cograph_read_file_range.

Use when: you have a node_id (from cograph_search_code, cograph_retrieve or cograph_related) and need its code. Prefer it to cograph_read_file_range for a whole function: it returns exactly the node, no guessed line window.

Do NOT use to search by name (use cograph_search_code) or to explore neighbours by graph (use cograph_related). Pass with_graph=true / with_summary=true / with_linked_docs=true only when you actually need the heavier payload — defaults skip them to keep tokens bounded.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | — |
| `node_id` | uuid | yes | — | — |
| `with_graph` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `with_summary` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `with_linked_docs` | boolean | no | `false` | — |
| `snippet_chars` | integer | no | `6000` | 80–16000 |

### `cograph_read_file_range`

Read a 1-indexed line range of a source file by repo slug + path.

Use when: you have a file path (typically `at` on a cograph_retrieve / cograph_search_code hit, or `provenance` on a cograph_read_node result) and need the lines around a hit that a node-bounded read won't capture. Aim at the hit: start ~20 lines above its start line and stop ~20 below its end line; do not start at line 1 unless you need the imports. Do not re-read lines already in your context.

Do NOT use to read one function or type (use cograph_read_node — exact body, no guessed window), to guess a path you have not seen in a result, to dump whole files (the range is capped at 1000 lines) or to search by content (use cograph_retrieve).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | — |
| `path` | string | yes | — | — |
| `start_line` | integer | yes | — | ≥ 1 |
| `end_line` | integer | yes | — | ≥ 1 |

- `end_line` must be greater than or equal to `start_line`, and `end_line - start_line + 1` must not exceed 1000 — the cap is on the span, not on either endpoint.
- An `end_line` past the end of the file is clamped rather than rejected, and the response reports it via `content_truncated`.

### `cograph_wiki_page`

Read ONE generated-wiki page — or a single named section of it — on demand. The body is cut at a line boundary after 12000 characters with structure preserved; `content_truncated` says whether that happened, and the fix is to re-read one `section` rather than to retry the page.

Use when: you need a generated-wiki page's prose, diagrams, or code samples. `page` is a slug from a search result's `wiki` or from cograph_outline's `wiki_pages`; pass `section` (a heading from that page's `sections` list) to pull just that section and save tokens.

Do NOT use to search code (use cograph_retrieve / cograph_search_code).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | — |
| `page` | string | yes | — | — |
| `section` | string | no | — | — |

### `cograph_collection_document`

Read one full markdown collection document with parsed metadata (headings, code blocks, tables, links). A document over 12000 characters is cut on a chunk boundary, without the metadata; continue with cograph_read_chunk(next_chunk_id).

Use when: agent has a known document_id from a prior cograph_collection_search / cograph_outline call.

Do NOT use to find documents (use cograph_collection_search) or to read just one chunk (use cograph_read_chunk — cheaper).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collection_id` | uuid | yes | — | — |
| `document_id` | uuid | yes | — | — |

### `cograph_read_chunk`

Fetch the full content of one markdown collection chunk by id.

Use when: cograph_collection_search returned a hit with content_truncated=true and the agent needs the rest of the chunk.

Do NOT use to read whole documents (use cograph_collection_document) or chunks from a different collection — chunk_id is scoped to its collection by access check.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `collection_id` | uuid | yes | — | — |
| `chunk_id` | uuid | yes | — | — |

## Traverse

Follow the code graph outwards from a node.

### `cograph_related`

Traverse the caller/callee graph around a code node up to `depth` hops (max 2).

Returns nodes and edges, scoped by `direction` (callers, callees, or both), capped at 50 nodes. `truncated: true` means the neighbourhood exceeded the cap — narrow with `direction` or continue from a more specific node instead of asking for more.

Use when: you have a node_id (from cograph_search_code or cograph_retrieve) and need what calls it or what it calls. If the question is how something is set or used and the hit is only a helper, read its callers; if the hit is a test, read its callees.

Do NOT use to find nodes by name (use cograph_search_code) or to read a node's body (use cograph_read_node).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Bounds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | string | yes | — | — |
| `node_id` | uuid | yes | — | — |
| `depth` | integer | no | `1` | 1–2 |
| `direction` | `callers` \| `callees` \| `both` | no | `both` | — |
